outcome: Emergency department visits for respiratory problems
finding: Infants delivered at hospitals with higher C-section rates had better health outcomes at birth, lower readmission rates, and suggestive evidence of improved survival, but were more likely to visit the emergency department for respiratory problems.
mod_finding: Infants delivered at hospitals with higher C-section rates experienced benefits driven by avoidance of prolonged labor but also had an increased risk of respiratory problems, consistent with an association between C-section and chronic respiratory health issues.
